full_judgment:
3. The short fact of the plaintiff's case is that the suit property belonged to one Kiran Lal Das who took over draft facility of Tk. 10(ten) thousand from Laljee and Sundarjee Bank Ltd., of Khatunganj, Chittagong on 20-5-1959 and created equitable mortgage of the said property by depositing the title deeds. Due to non-payment of loan liabilities, Bank filed Mortgage Suit on 29-3-1965 in preliminary form and final decree on 15-6-1966 and the said decree was put to execution by the Bank on 10-8-1966 in Execution Case No. 80 of 1966. Defendant-Government appeared in the said execution case and filed objection under Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Miscellaneous Case was upon the objection of the Government was started being Misc. Judicial Case No. 1366 of 1966 which was dismissed on 1-7-67. Thereafter the suit property was put to auction sale on 14-9-1967 in presence of the Government and plaintiffs vendor S.M. Bani Das (Proforma-defendant No. 3) purchased the suit property in auction sale which was confirmed on 30.10.67 and delivery of possession was given to auction purchaser to S.M. Bani Das on 18.11.67. Meanwhile E.P.Case No. 34/65-66 and 35/65-66 were started in respect of the said property but the learned R.D.C. after hearing the parties and on perusing the record held that it is not an Enemy Property and that auction purchaser Bani Das has acquired valid title by auction purchase and he was also pleased to recommend by his order dated 18.12.69 to drop the case. S.M. Bani Das thus mutated her name and paid rent and while she was the exclusive owner of the suit property, she sold the suit property to the plaintiffs who were her monthly tenants for valuable consideration by Registered Sale Deed No. 6707 dated 22.12.72 and Registered Sale Deed No. 1096 dated 23-1-73. Thereafter the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit property purchased for valuable consideration. So the plaintiffs have challenged the impugned notices dated 6.12.94 as illegal, malafide, void and inoperative and hence liable to be discharged. 

 8. Dr. Rafiqur Rahman with Mr. Emaduddin Chowdhury, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioner submits that the learned appellate Court is absolutely wrong and erroneous in his finding in allowing the appeal by bringing some modification in the judgment of the trial Court. The learned trial Court was absolutely right and justified in decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff, because the plaintiff by producing all the papers, documents, title deeds proved the title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land. The plaintiffs successfully proved their possession and title since their purchase from Bani Das and S.M. Bani Das purchase the suit land by auction purchase on 14-9-67. The learned Counsel further submits that the cause of auction for filing the suit arose on 6.12.74 when the Enemy Property authority served the notice upon the plaintiff to declare the property as Enemy Property. Thereafter the plaintiff was constrained to file the suit for declaration of title and also for declaring the notice dated 6.12.74 served upon the plaintiff is illegal, void, malafide, ultravires, inoperative and sought for permanent injunction. The trial Court decreed the suit as prayed for by the plaintiff because the plaintiff has been able to prove his title and possession in the suit land. Next he submits that the appellate Court also concurrently found that the plaintiff has been able to prove his title and possession in the suit land. But in spite of the modification of the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court is absolutely redundant and not sustainable under in law. The learned Counsel finally submits that since the law of Enemy Property itself died with the repeal of Ordinance No. 1 of 1969 on 23-3-1974 no further Vested Property case can be started thereafter on the basis of the law which is already dead. The learned Counsel in support of his contention referred the case of Aroti Rani Paul -Vs- Sudarshan Kumar Paul and others reported in 56 D.L.R (A.D) 73. He also submits that after the repeal of Ordinance No. 1 of 1969 on 23-3-1974 notice served upon the plaintiff on 6-12-74 was absolutely void, illegal, ultravires and not binding upon the plaintiff. The trial Court in his judgment properly and correctly declared that the notice dated 6.12.74 is illegal, ultravires, malafide and ineffective because the notice was served upon the plaintiff after the repeal of the Ordinance No. 1 of 1969. Before concluding his argument the learned Counsel submits that the lower appellate Court without applying his judicial mind and proper assessment of the documentary evidence particularly Emergency Provisions (Repeal) Act (XLV of 1974) which was promulgated earlier and the notice served upon the plaintiff after the promulgation and came to a wrong and preposterous finding occasioning failure of justice by reversing the appeal and modifying the judgment of the trial Court which is liable to be interfered by this Court, hence the rule should be made absolute. 

 9. Mr. Khondaker Aminul Hoque, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the opposite parties (Government) submits that the finding of the lower appellate Court is final in revision unless it is vitiated by non-consideration and misreading of evidence. Since there is no misreading and non-consideration of evidence the judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate Court is proper and justified. He further submits that the plaintiff did not seek any consequential relief and as such the case is hit by Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the appellate Court rightly observed in his judgment that the suit is hit by Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The learned Assistant Attorney General finally submits that the judgment and decree passed by the learned lower appellate Court calls for no interference by this Court in revisional jurisdiction, hence the rule should be discharged. 

 11. In view of the discussion made above and the facts and legal position of the case the impugned judgment and decree dated 19-2-2002 and 25-2-2002 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Chittagong, in Other Class Appeal No. 130 of 1984 allowing the appeal and modifying the judgment and decree dated 4.12.83 and 11.12.83 respectively passed by the then First Court of Munsif, Sadar, Chittagon, in Other Class Suit No. 332 of 1974 is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court is hereby affirmed.
